title: Financial Risk and Returns Prediction with Modular Networked Learning

extraction.methodology_summary: The paper builds an artificial agent using a Modular Networked Learning (MNL) system comprising interconnected recurrent neural networks (either LSTM or GRU). The main prediction unit (MPU) forecasts the next period's returns based on a past time window of returns, while a dispersion prediction unit (DPU) forecasts the next period's squared deviation around the MPU's prediction using a sliding window working memory block of past squared errors. These two conditional expectations are combined into a volatility-sensitive interval prediction for financial returns and tested across varying time window sizes.
extraction.data_period: S&P 500: Jan 3, 1950 - Jan 4, 2018 (8000 training, 9112 testing); NASDAQ: Feb 5, 1971 - Jan 4, 2018 (5000 training, 6834 testing); Russell 2000: Sep 10, 1987 - Jan 4, 2018 (3500 training, 4142 testing); daily
extraction.universe: S&P 500, NASDAQ Composite, and Russell 2000 dividend adjusted closing value indices

key_findings: Modular Networked Learning (MNL) agents can predict financial returns and market volatility simultaneously using interconnected recurrent neural network modules.

For GRU-based MNL systems, increasing the historical time window size improves interval prediction accuracy, achieving over 80% success rate at a 30-day window and up to ~98% success when using 2 standard deviation bounds.

The empirical results challenge the Efficient Market Hypothesis (EMH) by showing that past returns and volatility patterns contain predictable information that can be successfully exploited over long out-of-sample periods.
GRU architectures outperform LSTM architectures in capturing large market jumps, volatility bursts, and laminar periods within the proposed MNL framework.
